artifact.title: Spatial Environments — AI-First Browser Computing Foundation

scope.purpose: Enable an AI to understand, review, implement, test, and later resume construction of a browser-native screen-spatial computing environment without losing the reasoning in the source book.
does_not_apply_to: surfaces that are clearer as pages
scope.core_claim: A spatial interface is a persistent information model that can be viewed, navigated, manipulated, shared, and flattened without changing what the information means.
scope.target_platform: ordinary browser on an ordinary display
scope.non_goal: A decorative 3D desktop, game engine, or headset-dependent interface.

ingestion_order: build_contract or review_contract according to task
source_book sections when rationale or ambiguity needs resolution

precedence.authority: safety, accessibility, privacy, data integrity, and explicit user authority
constitutional invariants and normative MUST or MUST_NOT rules
spatial grammar, state ownership, and transaction contracts

do: Distinguish observed, inferred, proposed, implemented, and verified states.
Attach each finding or implementation claim to rule IDs and concrete evidence.
Record missing evidence as an evidence gap rather than inventing compliance.
Preserve existing interfaces and state unless the change is declared and reviewed.
Update the build-state checkpoint after verified work.
do_not: Infer canonical truth from layout, transforms, or screenshot coordinates.
Declare conformance from source inspection alone when runtime behavior matters.
Collapse personal view, shared session, and canonical truth into one store.
Resume from prose memory when a build-state checkpoint exists.

procedure: Resolve the implementation revision and evidence set.
Select claimed conformance classes and applicable rule IDs.
Review state ownership and destructive boundaries first.
Review behavior and runtime evidence second.
Establish or load a build-state checkpoint.
Implement the smallest complete reference slice in checkpoint order.
Keep the flat projection and semantic model live throughout construction.
Run acceptance tests before advancing a checkpoint.
Record decisions, evidence, unresolved findings, and next actions.
Verify the foundation version and SHA recorded in the checkpoint.
Verify repository, branch, revision, dependencies, and preview state.
Read verified capabilities and do_not_repeat before modifying anything.
Continue from the first unverified exit criterion, not from the beginning.

task_request_templates.review: Load this foundation, resolve the subject revision and claimed conformance classes, review only from named evidence, cite every finding to normative rule IDs, record unverified rules as evidence gaps, and return JSON conforming to review_contract.output_schema.
task_request_templates.build: Load this foundation and a build-state checkpoint, verify their versions and hashes, implement the current checkpoint as a complete vertical slice, preserve all mandatory invariants, run its exit criteria, and update decisions, evidence, findings, next actions, and handoff before stopping.
task_request_templates.resume: Load this foundation and the latest build-state checkpoint, verify repository and environment state, do not repeat verified work, revalidate stale evidence, and continue from the first unverified exit criterion while preserving rule and evidence IDs.
task_request_templates.performance_audit: Review the named runtime against RUNTIME-008 through RUNTIME-017 and the performance acceptance tests; require trace evidence for idle work, long tasks, frame-cap protection, cancelled loading, optional module loading, drawing-buffer bounds, and adaptive degradation.

normative_vocabulary.MUST: Required for the claimed scope or conformance class.
normative_vocabulary.MUST_NOT: Prohibited for the claimed scope or conformance class.
normative_vocabulary.SHOULD: Expected unless a documented, tested reason justifies an alternative.
normative_vocabulary.SHOULD_NOT: Avoid unless a documented, tested reason justifies it.
normative_vocabulary.MAY: Optional behavior that must not break mandatory invariants.

evidence_states.observed: Directly inspected in the named revision or runtime.
evidence_states.inferred: Reasonable conclusion that still requires verification.
evidence_states.proposed: A future design or change with no implementation claim.
evidence_states.implemented: Present in source or configuration but not necessarily runtime-verified.
evidence_states.verified: Demonstrated by named test or trace evidence.

framework_kernel.question: What is true?
framework_kernel.rule: Identity, provenance, permissions, and history do not live in pixels.

framework_kernel.question: Where does it appear?
framework_kernel.rule: One object may have several placements without becoming several objects.

framework_kernel.question: What moves together?
framework_kernel.rule: Batch layout and depth actions operate on groups and their placements.

framework_kernel.question: What can I manipulate now?
framework_kernel.rule: Window-like view state is separate from object lifecycle.

framework_kernel.question: What am I standing in?
framework_kernel.rule: A space is a named node in the session's semantic graph.

framework_kernel.question: What work must remain coherent?
framework_kernel.rule: Goal, snapshot, authority, actors, history, and return contract define continuity.

framework_kernel.question: What receives attention?
framework_kernel.rule: Camera clarity, selection, input focus, and shared attention remain distinct.

framework_kernel.question: What never leaves reach?
framework_kernel.rule: Safety, navigation, agent, and recovery instruments remain camera-fixed.

framework_kernel.question: What changes state?
framework_kernel.rule: Intent, preview, validation, authority, commit, explanation, record, and recovery govern change.

invariants: nested membership does not create nested depth
several placements may reference one object
view lifecycle does not change object lifecycle
human and AI share authorship model

state_boundaries.warning: View state, entity state, runtime tier, focus layer, and semantic depth are independent dimensions.

channel_map.x: local projection of neighboring space or composition
channel_map.color: status, actor, or category according to a declared legend
channel_map.time: dedicated history, playback, or forecast control

focus_stop_rules: one occupied stop per meaningful group
semantic state snaps even if motion interpolates
blur is optional optics rather than the definition of focus

focus_stack.question: Which session and space am I operating in?
Which stop and group are optically and semantically at z0?
Which frame, placement, object, or link is selected for action?
Which DOM element receives keyboard input?
What are collaborators or agents pointing at or acting on?

navigation.topology: typed space graph independent of coordinates
navigation.preview: yaw may reveal one chosen adjacency without committing location
navigation.commit: portal travel updates the spatial address and settles facing forward
navigation.local: pan between adjacent spaces and dolly between occupied group stops
navigation.long_distance: search, history, map, or command jump with compressed transition and return path
input_rules: do not reserve keys owned by text or assistive technology

verbs.travel: move camera to a space or occupied depth stop
verbs.open: create the one tethered detail layer
verbs.compare: assemble selected objects into a temporary focal slab
verbs.place: create another synchronized placement of an object
verbs.remove_placement: remove one appearance without deleting its object
verbs.restore: return to exact stored position and group cell
verbs.raise: change occlusion order without semantic depth change
verbs.resize_view: change presentation bounds and reflow content
verbs.close_view: remove an active representation while preserving object truth
verbs.pack_unpack_group: compact and restore a working set
verbs.trace: reveal provenance, dependency, or action path
verbs.recenter: return camera to a safe home view

accessibility_projection.flat_mode: complete equivalent projection of the same model
required: programmatic focus independent of camera focus
accessibility_projection.reduced_motion_effect: discrete state swaps with minimal fades or none; no travel, blur animation, tilt, or ambient loops

interaction_states.expression: progress attached to target object or group
ghost objects, links, or layout with difference preview
local result plus durable action record
failure at action site with unchanged state explicit

locus_policy.lens_assistant: personal command, search, explanation, navigation suggestion
locus_policy.object_tool: one bounded transformation, analysis, or explanation
locus_policy.group_agent: bounded task across one working set
locus_policy.external_service: action outside the environment with explicit destination and authority boundary

authority_invariants: AI may arrange attention but not rewrite truth
layout adoption and link adoption are separate transactions
external actions require named destination and receipt
stop remains visible while work runs

integration_contract.scope: Platform-neutral boundaries between the browser models, transaction engine, projections, persistence adapter, collaboration adapter, and optional graphics adapters. Network protocols and vendor APIs remain implementation decisions.

required_fields.transaction_id: stable identity shared by retries and lifecycle events
required_fields.phase: intent | preview | validate | authorize | commit | announce | record | recover
required_fields.target_refs: object, placement, frame, group, space, link, or external destination references
required_fields.authority_ref: permission or approval used for this phase
required_fields.status: pending | accepted | rejected | committed | cancelled | failed | recovered

conditional_fields.preview_diff: required before consequential shared, canonical, or external commit
conditional_fields.validation_result: required for validate and later phases
conditional_fields.commit_versions: required after durable shared or canonical commit
conditional_fields.receipt: required after an external action is accepted by its destination
conditional_fields.failure: required for failed status and must name unchanged and uncertain state
conditional_fields.recovery_ref: required when undo, retry, revert, or reconciliation is available

idempotency.rule: Every mutating commit uses a stable transaction_id and an idempotency key scoped to destination and intended mutation.
idempotency.duplicate_behavior: A duplicate commit returns or references the original outcome; it does not produce another mutation, action record, external send, or receipt.
idempotency.retry_behavior: Retries revalidate authority, current versions, intent, and staleness before commit.
idempotency.view_exception: Pure personal-view changes may be coalesced and need not create durable cross-device events unless persistence or collaboration requires them.

failure_semantics.cancelled_before_commit: No durable mutation; remove ephemeral previews and restore the stable source state.
failure_semantics.validation_failed: Anchor errors to the target; retain user input and unchanged canonical state.
failure_semantics.authority_failed: Name the missing or expired authority and preserve all state.
failure_semantics.version_conflict: Do not overwrite; expose current version, proposed diff, and resolution path.
failure_semantics.commit_outcome_unknown: Freeze duplicate attempts, reconcile by transaction_id, and distinguish unknown from failed.
failure_semantics.external_action_failed: Name destination and failure; never imply completion without a receipt.
failure_semantics.projection_failed: Fall back to a semantic flat or static representation without changing model state.

persistence_boundary.canonical_store: Objects, declared links, versions, provenance, permissions, and domain history.
persistence_boundary.session_store: Goal, snapshot, space graph, published topology, actors, action timeline, undo and return contract.
persistence_boundary.personal_view_store: Camera, focus stack, local placements, frames, lens and performance preferences, resume capsule.
persistence_boundary.ephemeral_store: Transaction-scoped previews and gestures only; never restored as truth.

rendering_policy.canvas_2d: dense relationship fields and non-semantic atmosphere when SVG cost is material
rendering_policy.gsap: optional adapter for interruption, scrubbing, FLIP, or coordinated timelines; never owns state
rendering_policy.three_js: dynamic optional surface for genuine meshes, occlusion, model inspection, shaders, or volumetric content
rendering_policy.idle_invariant: zero requested animation frames and zero optional rendering work after settlement

rules: animate a world or group root instead of all members
separate geometry reads from style writes
add will-change only around known motion
stop loops in hidden, frozen, minimized, or settled states

controls.meaning: amount of atmosphere, optics, and optional graphics
maximum fully live readable or interactive DOM frames
how far beyond current attention full or partial representations prepare

notes: effect and 3D assets begin only on intent or qualified idle

custom_combinations.constraint: must satisfy the same certified interaction and accessibility budgets

performance.accessibility_precedence: prefers-reduced-motion and equivalent accessibility requirements override speed or richness preferences
interaction_certification: no interaction-time main-thread task longer than 50 ms
declared frame budget held in trace

frame_capacity.counted: fully live DOM frames with readable or interactive contents

runtime_tiers.warm: mounted for imminent promotion, inert, no media or loops
runtime_tiers.frozen: lightweight labeled snapshot with exact state preserved in model
runtime_tiers.minimized: lens chip and persisted state only

reclamation_order: freeze least-recently-used clean inactive eligible frame
minimize it if the profile does not retain frozen snapshots
frame_capacity.all_protected_behavior: pause opening and ask for an explicit eligible frame to park; never close, delete, discard, or terminate work

loading.invariant: virtualization and loading never change identity, history, searchability, permissions, or session continuity

degradation_order: reduce shadow, backdrop area, and resting blur
lower Canvas or WebGL drawing-buffer resolution
simplify or freeze non-focal relationship drawing
freeze warm neighbors and shorten loading horizon
replace optional volumetric scenery with static projection
adaptive_quality.announcement: announce one temporary downshift and offer Restore or Keep Efficient
adaptive_quality.recovery: wait until next session or explicit request to avoid oscillation

normative_rule_registry.statement: Every spatial effect must answer an operator question about location, relationships, change, action, AI activity, authorship, or return.
normative_rule_registry.validation: For each effect, record at least one operator question it answers.

normative_rule_registry.statement: World, personal camera, and lens state must remain distinct.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Inspect the state model and prove separate owners and persistence lifetimes.

normative_rule_registry.statement: One participant's camera movement must not move another participant unless explicit escapable follow mode is active.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Run a two-participant camera-independence test.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Every spatial surface must have a flat comparison or prior baseline and must earn depth through measurable task value.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Compare completion, error, context recovery, and comprehension against the baseline.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Named locations, stable addresses, predictable adjacency, landmarks, return paths, and overview must exist independently of scenery.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Disable visual atmosphere and verify navigation remains coherent.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Each visual channel must have one declared semantic meaning at environment scope.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Audit x, y, z, containment, edges, portals, color, motion, and time against the environment legend.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Object truth, placement appearance, frame view state, and representation level must be modeled separately.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Open the same object in two placements and verify one canonical identity and history.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Inferred spatial relationships must remain tentative until explicitly adopted as typed links.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Reject a proposed relationship and prove canonical truth did not change.

normative_rule_registry.statement: The z-axis must encode attention and interaction availability only.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Inspect every occupied depth and confirm it does not encode chronology, certainty, seniority, hierarchy, or similarity.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Depth must use discrete z0 through z3 semantic rings with no more than three rings behind focus.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Enumerate occupied stops and confirm conformance to the depth-state table.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Readable body text must not exist outside z0.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Traverse every stop and test computed visibility, inertness, and readable content.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Representation detail must change semantically with distance rather than rendering miniature full interfaces.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Compare z0 through z3 representations for each core object type.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Every reversible departure must retain identity, origin, and exact restoration.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Exercise minimize, periscope, detail, group move, and AI preview then verify exact return.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Object and placement addresses must be serializable, linkable, restorable, permission-safe, and convertible to flat routes.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Refresh deep links to an object and a placement and verify correct recovery.

normative_rule_registry.statement: The lens must expose address, overview, depth position, home, history, search, and visible destinations.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Navigate without gestures and confirm every required instrument remains reachable.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Results and failures must appear at the object, group, or task where the action occurred.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Execute local and external actions and inspect causal feedback at the action site.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Consequential direct manipulation must provide preview, valid targets, non-drag alternatives, deterministic snap, undo, conflict handling, and promised restoration.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Complete equivalent pointer and keyboard workflows including conflict and undo.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Use world objects, world annotations, lens instruments, and temporary lens incidents according to their semantic role.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Classify every persistent interface element into one declared role.

normative_rule_registry.statement: AI state must expose listening, working, proposing, waiting, committed, and failed conditions where applicable.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Observe a complete agent lifecycle and verify state, task, stop, and outcome are inspectable.

normative_rule_registry.statement: AI must not silently convert inference into evidence, hide counterevidence, approve, mutate shared truth, or erase another participant's arrangement.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Attempt each prohibited operation without authority and verify rejection plus unchanged state.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Shared objects and declared topology must be synchronized while cameras and uncommitted arrangements remain personal by default.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Compare two participants' world and view state before and after local arrangement changes.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Motion must explain causality with one dominant coordinated event and restrained camera amplitude.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Record state transitions and identify one dominant motion family per event.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Legibility, action reachability, and redundant state cues must outrank physical realism.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Test zoom, contrast, occlusion, edge tilt, blur-disabled mode, and small viewports.

normative_rule_registry.statement: The active view must expose one dominant task and primary action with bounded live signals and no more than one tethered overlay.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Count competing primary tasks, overlays, and actionable signals at rest.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Flat mode must be an equivalent projection of the same entities, relationships, state, actions, authorship, history, and return paths.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Complete the same reference workflow in spatial and flat projections.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Each implementation must declare baseline hardware, interaction budget, object and connector limits, virtualization thresholds, degradation order, and memory recovery.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Inspect the performance certification manifest and trace evidence.

normative_rule_registry.statement: The authoritative world, session, personal view, frames, focus, collaboration, AI proposals, history, and schema version must be serializable and replayable.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Round-trip a populated session through persistence and compare identities and state.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Privacy, sharing, agent scope, external destinations, recording, and authority boundaries must be visible without leaking hidden content.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Test unauthorized links, presence, search, and topology for side-channel leakage.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Spatial success must be measured by task evidence rather than perceived futurism.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Collect the named task and collaboration metrics against a baseline.

normative_rule_registry.statement: A resume capsule must distinguish prior personal view from current shared truth and offer explicit restore-view and catch-up paths.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Interrupt, mutate shared state elsewhere, and test both return verbs.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Environment, session, space, group, placement, object, link, portal, frame, plane, lens, and actor must be distinct primitives.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Inspect schema identity types and reject ambiguous IDs.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Every state field must declare canonical-truth, shared-session, personal-view, or ephemeral-interaction ownership.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Generate a field ownership report with no unclassified fields.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Context, camera, work, input, and shared-attention focus must remain independently inspectable.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Change each focus layer independently and verify no unexplained focus theft.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Focus, travel, open, compare, place, remove placement, park, minimize, restore, raise, resize view, close view, move view, group operations, publish arrangement, link, trace, and recenter must preserve their declared targets and authority.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Audit action events for verb, target type, owner plane, authority, and undo boundary.

normative_rule_registry.statement: The group, not an individual card or frame, is the atomic persistent depth unit.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Verify every placement inherits world depth from an explicit group.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Every group must declare tile, stack, canvas, graph, sequence, or another specified layout policy with deterministic behavior.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Resize and batch-operate every supported layout mode.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Links must be typed, named, provenance-aware, accessible without color alone, and renderable in flat mode.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Inspect, select, trace, and flatten declared and tentative edges.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Spaces must form a semantic graph of typed portals independent of projected coordinates.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Reproject neighbors and verify graph identity and portal routing are unchanged.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Loading, unloading, yaw, camera angle, or rendering distance must not create or end a session.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Virtualize the entire non-current neighborhood and verify the continuity contract remains.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Wheel-to-dolly may operate only in an explicitly focused spatial stage with a release path and non-wheel alternative.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Test first interaction, Esc release, page scroll, assistive technology, and visible controls.

normative_rule_registry.statement: A session must declare goal, success condition, scope, authority, participants, topology, history root, resume capsule, and exit contract.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Validate every session manifest against required fields.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Opened-on-top may create only one tethered detail layer and must restore source camera, focus, selection, and internal scroll exactly.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Open and close detail from multiple source states and compare checkpoints.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Periscope, minimize, close view, and delete entity must remain distinct states and actions.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Exercise each action and verify object truth and recovery semantics.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Safety-persistent and navigation-persistent lens controls must remain reachable and must never inherit world blur, tilt, recession, or occlusion.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Move through every camera state and inspect lens transform, focus, and reachability.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Every transition must declare one motion family: acknowledge, promote/recede, travel, tether, park/restore, transfer, preview/commit, or incident.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Inspect the motion token and event mapping.

normative_rule_registry.statement: An AI proposal must preserve proposer, model/runtime label where relevant, time, targets, action, sources, uncertainty, preview, authority, staleness, decision, decision-maker, and result.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Validate proposal objects before preview and commit.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Every agent must reveal its human or organizational principal, goal, locus, scope, tools, mutation rights, budget, and stop condition.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Inspect the roster and action record for every active agent.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Pointing and shared attention must identify object, placement when relevant, and version rather than raw screen coordinates alone.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Share attention across different viewport sizes and camera positions.

normative_rule_registry.statement: AI commits must participate in the same version, history, concurrency, conflict, and recovery rules as human commits.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Create a human/AI concurrent edit and resolve it at object or field level.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Every actor must use intent, preview, validate, authorize, commit, announce, record, and recover with rigor proportional to consequence.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Trace view, shared-arrangement, canonical-content, and external-action transactions.

normative_rule_registry.statement: The runtime must be model-first; DOM position and transform strings must not be the data model.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Reconstruct the same state in flat and spatial projections from serialized models.

normative_rule_registry.statement: CSS 3D must be treated as a projection of flat planes with explicit semantic focus and hit testing.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Test transformed overlap, backfaces, keyboard order, and pointer routing in supported browsers.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Filters, opacity, clipping, masking, overflow, and glass must not silently flatten required preserve-3d subtrees.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Run cross-browser scene-flattening fixtures for every grouping property used.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Readable, focusable, editable, and actionable work must remain semantic DOM; graphics layers may render atmosphere, dense edges, or genuine 3D with semantic equivalents.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Disable graphics layers and complete the core workflow through DOM and flat projection.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Responsive behavior must choose an equivalent projection rather than shrinking the room and its controls.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Test wide, compact, narrow/touch, reduced-motion, and flat projections.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Browser history must represent meaningful destinations, not transient hover or every camera pixel.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Exercise back/forward after navigation, detail, focus, and drag operations.

normative_rule_registry.statement: The default core should use semantic DOM, CSS transforms, Web Animations, sparse SVG, and optional Canvas; GSAP is an adapter and Three.js is dynamically imported only for genuine volumetric needs.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Inspect the initial bundle and dependency graph.

normative_rule_registry.statement: The settled environment must request zero animation frames and own no Canvas, WebGL, media, or ambient rendering loop.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Record a settled performance trace and count requested frames and timers.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Visual richness, active-frame capacity, and loading horizon must be independent personal-view controls.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Adjust each control independently without reload or truth mutation.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Efficient, Balanced, and Cinematic presets must exist, with Balanced as default and accessibility preferences taking precedence.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Switch through presets and verify exact values, persistence, announcement, and reduced-motion precedence.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Frame caps must count fully live frames, preserve model records, and reclaim only eligible clean inactive views through freeze or minimize.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Exceed each preset cap with mixed eligible and protected frames.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Pinned, dirty, invalid, approval, transfer, recording, external-preview, focus-source, or running-transaction frames must not be reclaimed automatically.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Mark each protected condition and force capacity pressure.

normative_rule_registry.statement: When all frames are protected, opening must pause for an explicit capacity choice rather than close, delete, discard, or terminate work.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Fill the cap entirely with protected frames and attempt another open.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Content must load through Now, Next, Later, and Cold priorities derived from semantic intent, with cancellable speculative work and stale-response guards.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Rapidly change intent and verify cancelled or stale responses cannot mutate the view.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Adaptive degradation must remove atmosphere before information in a deterministic announced order and must not oscillate during work.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Trigger a downshift and inspect order, user notice, reversibility, and semantic parity.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Canvas and Three.js must render on demand; WebGL drawing-buffer pixels must be capped independently of full device pixel ratio.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Open, settle, hide, and close optional graphics while tracing frames, pixels, and resource disposal.

normative_rule_registry.statement: Certified interaction traces must avoid main-thread tasks longer than 50 ms, hold the declared frame budget, preserve focus under CPU throttling, and return to zero optional work when hidden.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Capture traces on named baseline hardware and throttled profiles.

normative_rule_registry.statement: A claimed conformance class must satisfy every requirement and acceptance test assigned to that class.
normative_rule_registry.validation: Produce a rule-to-evidence matrix with no unverified mandatory rows.

conformance.claim_rule: A class may be claimed only when every applicable mandatory rule and acceptance test has named evidence.

acceptance_tests.assertion: Every rendered object resolves to one model identity.
The same object can appear in two placements without duplicated truth, history, or actions.
Closing or removing one placement leaves the object and its other placements intact.
Every relationship is either declared or visibly tentative.
Every card or frame resolves through a placement to one explicit group or to the one temporary detail layer; no placement stores an arbitrary persistent world depth.
Every field can be attributed to canonical, shared-session, personal-view, or ephemeral-interaction state.
Group, placement, frame, view, and entity state remain independently inspectable.
Every object and placement address restores after refresh.
Back/forward returns to the expected durable states.
Keyboard-only users can enter, navigate, operate, and leave the stage.
Recenter is always available.
Long jumps preserve origin and return.
Wheel capture never traps the page or browser.
Yaw preview does not silently commit space travel, and a committed neighboring space settles facing forward.
The semantic space graph remains correct when the renderer projects different neighbors or coordinates.
Loading and unloading a virtualized neighbor does not change session identity.
A session transition names the changed continuity contract, resolves scoped work and agents, and offers return.
Restoring a session distinguishes the prior personal view from shared changes that happened while away.
Only z0 contains readable body text.
Recessed surfaces are not accidentally focusable or clickable.
Every dolly input snaps to an occupied focus stop and clamps at both ends; no stable state leaves every group blurred.
Changing group depth preserves the focal group identity or announces the new focal target.
Opened-on-top restores camera, focus, selection, and source state exactly.
Programmatic focus is correct even when camera focus changes.
Context, camera, work, input, and shared-attention focus can be inspected independently and never steal one another implicitly.
Move, raise, stack, resize, periscope, minimize, restore, and close produce the declared view states without changing entity truth.
Resize reflows or changes semantic representation; it never bitmap-scales readable UI.
Close view and delete entity are distinct verbs with distinct authority and recovery.
Tile, stack, canvas, graph, and sequence groups either obey their declared layout policy or are rejected as unsupported; no silent fallback corrupts placement.
Safety-persistent lens controls remain reachable throughout camera motion and world focus changes.
Only z0 world controls enter the active world focus order; occluded and recessed views are inert.
Two participants can point to the same object despite different cameras.
Personal view changes do not mutate shared topology.
Follow mode is explicit and escapable.
Concurrent edits produce a visible resolution path.
The agent’s target, source scope, and current state are inspectable.
Consequential shared changes require the correct authority.
Proposal rejection leaves no mutation.
Commit creates an attributable history event.
Stop, failure, and retry states are deterministic.
Each agent reveals principal, goal, locus, scope, budget, and stop condition.
A layout proposal, shared-arrangement publication, canonical link adoption, and external action remain separate transactions.
View, shared-arrangement, canonical-content, and external transactions enforce different authority without changing the interaction vocabulary.
Cancel before commit leaves no durable mutation.
Commit produces a local causal result, version, authorship, and recoverable record.
Interrupted drag, camera travel, session portal, and agent commit settle into one deterministic state.
Resume after refresh, disconnect, or device handoff does not duplicate actions or discard unreconciled work.
Flat mode contains every entity, relationship, state, and action.
All drag actions have single-pointer and keyboard alternatives.
Pointer targets meet the selected WCAG level.
Reduced motion removes travel, blur animation, tilt, and ambient loops.
Screen-reader output does not duplicate visual mirror content.
Camera and drag interactions meet the declared frame budget on baseline hardware.
The settled environment owns no active animation frame, Canvas loop, WebGL loop, autoplaying media, or ambient timer.
Efficient, Balanced, and Cinematic can be selected without reload, state loss, or change to canonical or shared-session truth.
Each of the three performance controls can be adjusted independently and restored to its preset value.
Opening beyond the active-frame cap freezes or minimizes only an eligible clean inactive frame and restores it exactly later.
Pinned, dirty, approval, focus-source, and running-transaction frames are never reclaimed automatically.
If every frame is protected, opening pauses for an explicit capacity choice rather than closing or deleting anything.
Now, Next, Later, and Cold content priorities load only their declared representation and cancel stale speculative work.
Optional GSAP and Three.js modules are absent from the initial core path and load only when a requested projection requires them.
Optional Three.js rendering stops after settlement and caps its physical drawing-buffer resolution.
A performance downshift is visible, deterministic, reversible, and never removes semantic content, provenance, safety, or recovery controls.
Far spaces and hidden groups virtualize without breaking addresses or search.
The loaded neighborhood may change without resetting the session, collaboration context, or undo timeline.
Losing connection does not corrupt local or shared state.
Visual degradation removes atmosphere before information.

evaluation_scenarios.task: Find the evidence supporting a decision and identify its source.
Open a record, inspect it, and return without losing the prior comparison.
Explain the relationship between two distant objects.
Ask the AI to propose a cluster, reject one link, and publish the rest.
Invite a collaborator to the same object while keeping independent cameras.
Hand over presentation control and leave follow mode.
Complete the workflow using keyboard only and reduced motion.
Refresh from a shared link and recover the same durable state.
Group several cards, traverse every occupied focus stop, and confirm that no resting state leaves all useful content blurred.
Yaw toward a neighboring space, commit travel within the session, then use the portal to enter and return from a different session.
Move, stack, resize, minimize, close, and restore frames without changing or deleting their underlying objects.
Open the same object in two placements, change canonical state once, and confirm that both views reconcile without duplicate history.
Publish one personal placement while leaving another private; verify that a collaborator receives only the published arrangement.
Interrupt the session, change shared state from another participant, then test both restore-my-view and catch-me-up.
Move through context, camera, work, input, and shared-attention focus independently without an unexplained focus jump.
Ask the AI researcher to propose a layout and a relationship, accept only the layout, and verify that canonical truth remains unchanged.
Switch Efficient → Balanced → Cinematic → custom while preserving objects, placements, focus, history, and available actions.
Exceed the active-frame cap with clean, pinned, dirty, approval, focus-source, and running-agent frames; verify that only an eligible frame freezes or minimizes and every frame restores exactly.
Travel toward one neighbor and immediately choose another; verify that stale speculative loading cancels and cannot overwrite the new view.

Open and close the optional Three.js inspection, then prove that its module is absent from the initial path, its drawing buffer is capped, its loop stops after settlement, and its resources dispose on close.
Record the settled room and confirm zero requested animation frames and zero optional rendering work; record common motion sequences under the named baseline and throttled profiles.

minimum_reference_slice.name: Evidence and Decision Session
required_capabilities: Space A · Question — the decision, constraints, and open assumptions;
Space B · Evidence — source groups, claims, counterevidence, and provenance links;
Space C · Action — options, approval, owner, dependencies, and next proofs;
one explicit session goal, success condition, snapshot, authority scope, actor roster, and exit contract;
a three-node space graph with labeled portals and only the useful one-hop neighborhood fully rendered;
at least three groups using two different layout modes at distinct occupied focus stops;
one object deliberately shown in two placements, proving synchronized identity without duplicated truth;
one named portal to a second session with a return path;
one human collaborator and one bounded AI researcher;
separate context, camera, work, input, and shared-attention focus instrumentation;
one opened-on-top evidence inspection;
one temporary comparison slab;
one move, stack, resize, pack, minimize, and exact-restore frame sequence;
one tentative AI-proposed relationship;
one view transaction, one shared-arrangement publication, one canonical-content commit, and one mocked external-action preview;
one interruption, changed-while-away event, restore-view path, and catch-up path;
one lens performance console exposing visual richness, active-frame capacity, and loading horizon;
Efficient, Balanced, and Cinematic preset demonstrations plus one custom combination;
enough frames to exceed the Balanced cap, including pinned, dirty, approval, and running-agent protection cases;
observable Now, Next, Later, and Cold loading transitions with cancelled speculative work;
an optional dynamically imported Three.js object inspection that renders on demand and disposes cleanly;
a recorded idle state with zero animation, Canvas, WebGL, media, or ambient loops;
one flat-mode projection.

review_contract.objective: Determine conformance, correctness, safety, accessibility, performance, maintainability, and evidence sufficiency without mistaking visual polish for implementation truth.

severity_model.critical: Likely data loss, unauthorized mutation, privacy leak, inaccessible core workflow, corrupted shared truth, or unrecoverable state.
severity_model.high: Major correctness, interaction, performance, or conformance defect that blocks broad use.
severity_model.medium: Material weakness advisable to fix before scale-up or expansion.
severity_model.low: Bounded craft, hygiene, documentation, or maintainability improvement.

verdict_rules.conformant: All mandatory applicable rules verified; no unresolved critical or high findings.
verdict_rules.conformant_with_conditions: No critical findings; bounded high or medium findings have owners and do not invalidate the claimed class.
verdict_rules.not_conformant: A mandatory invariant fails or an unresolved critical finding exists.
verdict_rules.insufficient_evidence: Available material cannot verify the claimed behavior.

versioning_and_compatibility.artifact_version_policy: Major changes break entity meanings, ownership planes, transaction semantics, or mandatory rule interpretation. Minor changes add compatible capabilities or rules. Patch changes clarify wording, references, or validation without changing intent.
versioning_and_compatibility.checkpoint_requirement: Every build state records foundation artifact ID, version, and exact file SHA-256.
migration_procedure: Compare artifact versions and rule IDs.
Mark evidence stale when a referenced mandatory rule changed meaning or validation.
Migrate serialized data explicitly when entity, ownership, address, or transaction schemas changed.
Re-run affected checkpoint exit criteria and acceptance tests.
Record the migration as a build-state decision with before and after versions.
versioning_and_compatibility.backward_compatibility: A renderer may evolve without data migration when stable model identities, ownership, addresses, event semantics, and flat equivalence remain unchanged.

principle_index.abstract: A reusable system cannot mix universal principles, interaction semantics, brand art direction, and browser mechanics in one rule list. V3 has four layers.

principle_index.title: The person is an operator, not an audience
principle_index.abstract: Games and cinematic interfaces can look similar while serving opposite purposes. A film interface explains a character’s intent to an audience. A working interface must let a person form intent, predict an action, execute it, inspect the result, and recover from error.

principle_index.title: The viewport is a personal camera into a shared world

principle_index.title: Topology comes before atmosphere

principle_index.abstract: The z-axis answers: *How available is this object to act on now?*

principle_index.title: Semantic zoom accompanies geometric depth
principle_index.abstract: Distance does more than shrink an object. It changes what the object says.

principle_index.title: Object and placement permanence are the foundation of trust
principle_index.abstract: An object that moves must leave a comprehensible trace of where it came from and where it went.

principle_index.title: The result appears where the action happened
principle_index.abstract: Games are exceptionally good at local causality: the switch changes the door, the tool affects the object, and resource state lives close to its source.

principle_index.title: AI is present, bounded, and attributable
principle_index.abstract: The Tony Stark fantasy is not floating holograms. It is a tight loop between intent, computation, simulation, manipulation, and explanation.

principle_index.abstract: Collaboration synchronizes what must be common and leaves perspective personal.

principle_index.title: Presence attaches to attention and action
principle_index.abstract: A useful collaborator is more than an avatar bubble.

principle_index.title: Motion explains causality
principle_index.abstract: Motion is a grammatical device. It answers: what moved, why, from where, to where, and with what consequence?

principle_index.title: Legibility outranks physical realism
principle_index.abstract: The environment may suggest optics; it must not simulate them at the expense of use.

principle_index.title: Attention is a finite room resource
principle_index.abstract: The room may be infinite; attention is not.

principle_index.title: Accessibility is an equivalent projection
principle_index.abstract: Flat mode is not a visual fallback. It is another complete view of the same model.

principle_index.abstract: Dropped frames, delayed focus, and late hit testing make objects feel unreal and controls feel unsafe.

principle_index.abstract: Spatial memory matters most when attention leaves and later returns. The framework therefore treats interruption as a normal lifecycle event.

principle_index.abstract: Spatial systems fail when camera preferences, collaborative layout, business truth, and transient gestures share one undifferentiated state object. V3 requires four ownership planes.

principle_index.abstract: Depth cues use size, clarity, luminance, occlusion, and motion together, but no single cue is required to perceive the state.

principle_index.abstract: CSS transforms are well suited to browser-native 2.5D panels: shared perspective, translateZ, rotations, and readable DOM content. The standard is explicit that transformed elements remain flat planes, not volumetric objects. CSS Transforms Level 2

# Spatial Environments — Browser Computing Principles

**Reference-model revision · V3.1 · 19 July 2026**  
**Purpose:** a reusable grammar for spatial working environments that run in an ordinary browser on an ordinary display.  
**Applies to:** operational consoles, approval rooms, agent theatres, investigations, planning environments, and collaborative decision surfaces.  
**Does not apply to:** articles, reports, settings, long-form reading, routine forms, or any surface that is clearer as a page.

> A spatial interface is not a page with perspective. It is a persistent information model that can be viewed, navigated, manipulated, shared, and flattened without changing what the information means.

---

sections.title: Executive conclusion
The framework kernel
sections.source_markdown:
## The framework kernel

| Question | Authoritative unit | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| What is true? | Object and link | Identity, provenance, permissions, and history do not live in pixels. |
| Where does it appear? | Placement | One object may have several placements without becoming several objects. |
| What moves together? | Group | Batch layout and depth actions operate on groups and their placements. |
| What can I manipulate now? | Frame | Window-like view state is separate from object lifecycle. |
| What am I standing in? | Space | A named node in the session’s semantic space graph. |
| What work must remain coherent? | Session | Goal, snapshot, authority, collaborators, agents, history, and return contract. |
| What receives attention? | Focus stop and focus stack | Camera clarity, selection, keyboard focus, and shared attention remain distinct. |
| What never leaves reach? | Lens | Safety, navigation, agent, and recovery instruments stay camera-fixed. |
| What changes state? | Transaction | Intent, preview, validation, authority, commit, explanation, record, and recovery. |

This kernel is deliberately more precise than the visual metaphor. A renderer may look like a room, stage, gallery, constellation, shelf, or graph. Conformance depends on the model and verbs, not the scenery.

---

sections.title: 0 · Keep four layers separate
sections.source_markdown:
## 0 · Keep four layers separate

A reusable system cannot mix universal principles, interaction semantics, brand art direction, and browser mechanics in one rule list. V3 has four layers.

sections.title: Layer A — Constitution
sections.source_markdown:
### Layer A — Constitution

Stable principles that should survive a different brand, visual theme, rendering technology, input device, or screen size.

Examples: stable topology, object permanence, personal camera/shared world, bounded AI authority, semantic equivalence in flat mode.

sections.title: Layer B — Spatial grammar
sections.source_markdown:
### Layer B — Spatial grammar

Named primitives, states, relationships, navigation verbs, collaboration rules, and accessibility behavior.

Examples: sessions, space graphs, groups, placements, focus stack, frame states, portals, links, periscope, opened-on-top, and the transaction protocol.

sections.title: Layer C — Visual and motion profiles
sections.source_markdown:
### Layer C — Visual and motion profiles

An art direction that realizes the grammar. INTO’s off-centre vanishing point, petrol canvas, mono markers, glass recipe, edge tilt, and motion curve belong here.

These rules may be strict for INTO without pretending to be universal truths about spatial computing.

sections.title: Layer D — Implementation and conformance
sections.source_markdown:
### Layer D — Implementation and conformance

Browser architecture, performance budgets, semantic DOM requirements, state serialization, tests, and machine-checkable constraints.

This separation is the difference between a compelling prototype and a framework other products can safely adopt.

sections.title: Part I — Constitutional principles
sections.source_markdown: # Part I — Constitutional principles

sections.title: 1 · The person is an operator, not an audience
sections.source_markdown:
## 1 · The person is an operator, not an audience

Games and cinematic interfaces can look similar while serving opposite purposes. A film interface explains a character’s intent to an audience. A working interface must let a person form intent, predict an action, execute it, inspect the result, and recover from error.

Every spatial effect must answer at least one operator question:

- Where am I?
- What is related?
- What changed?
- What can I act on?
- What is the AI doing?
- Who changed this?
- How do I return?

If it answers none of them, it is production design, not interface design.

sections.title: 2 · The viewport is a personal camera into a shared world
sections.source_markdown:
## 2 · The viewport is a personal camera into a shared world

The founding inversion remains valid, with one refinement: the viewport is not the room and the camera is not shared state.

- The **world** contains objects, relationships, groups, agents, history, and spatial addresses.
- The **camera** contains one participant’s position, orientation, focus plane, zoom, and temporary view preferences.
- The **lens** contains instruments that must remain readable regardless of world movement.

In collaboration, participants normally share the world while keeping independent cameras. “Follow me” or presentation mode is an explicit, reversible choice; one person’s navigation never yanks everyone else through the room.

sections.title: 3 · The room must earn itself
sections.source_markdown:
## 3 · The room must earn itself

Depth is justified only when it improves one of four jobs:

1. preserving context during a detour;
2. making relationships or dependency structure easier to understand;
3. organizing concurrent work without losing object permanence; or
4. establishing shared reference for people and AI.

The system must have a flat baseline for comparison. If users are slower, more lost, or less accurate, simplify or flatten the experience. Spatial is a hypothesis to prove, not a brand entitlement.

sections.title: 4 · Topology comes before atmosphere
5 · One channel, one meaning
6 · Objects carry identity; placements and frames carry presentation
7 · Spatial arrangement is meaningful but never secret
sections.source_markdown:
## 7 · Spatial arrangement is meaningful but never secret

Proximity, alignment, containment, and repetition can express emerging structure. Spatial-hypertext research showed that people create interpretable relationships through layout and that systems can help turn implicit structure into explicit links. [Marshall and Shipman](https://people.engr.tamu.edu/shipman/viki/papers/ht93/ht93.html)

V3 therefore allows two kinds of relationship:

- **suggested relation:** inferred from proximity, repeated movement, shared sources, or AI analysis; shown as a tentative edge or grouping proposal;
- **declared relation:** explicitly typed, named, queryable, and preserved independently of layout.

AI may notice a pattern in the arrangement. It may not silently promote that pattern into organizational truth.

sections.title: 8 · Depth is attention, not storage
9 · Semantic zoom accompanies geometric depth
sections.source_markdown:
## 9 · Semantic zoom accompanies geometric depth

Distance does more than shrink an object. It changes what the object says.

- At z0, show the working representation.
- At z1, show identity, state, owner, and the one fact needed to decide whether to promote it.
- At z2, show group identity, count, trend, or exception signal.
- At z3, show only landmark, occupancy, or ambient health.

This is semantic zoom. It prevents unreadable miniature dashboards and makes the information hierarchy survive low resolution, narrow viewports, and flat mode.

Pad++ framed this more broadly as an “information physics”: useful representations should emerge predictably from interaction rules rather than from a literal desktop metaphor. V3 adopts that principle but snaps to meaningful stops because continuous zoom is not itself an information architecture. [Pad++](https://www.cs.umd.edu/~bederson/images/pubs_pdfs/p17-bederson.pdf)

sections.title: 10 · Object and placement permanence are the foundation of trust
sections.source_markdown:
## 10 · Object and placement permanence are the foundation of trust

An object that moves must leave a comprehensible trace of where it came from and where it went.

- Minimize preserves a dock identity.
- Periscope preserves an edge sliver.
- Moving a group preserves its placement membership and each placement’s object identity.
- Opening detail preserves the source context behind it.
- AI reorganization appears first as a preview.
- Closing or undoing restores the prior arrangement exactly.

Persistent placement—not three-dimensionality by itself—is what enables spatial memory. If the same object appears in more than one place, the system reveals that they are synchronized views of one identity and offers a route between placements.

sections.title: 11 · Objects and placements have different addresses; every journey has a return
sections.source_markdown:
## 11 · Objects and placements have different addresses; every journey has a return

The minimum **placement address** is:

`environment / session / space / group / placement`

The canonical **object address** is independent of presentation:

`environment / object`

An optional personal view capsule may add camera, focal stop, frame state, and selection to a deep link. Those parameters are never mistaken for the object’s identity or shared truth.

The address must be:

- serializable;
- linkable;
- restorable after refresh;
- represented in browser history where navigation semantics warrant it;
- shareable without exposing unauthorized content; and
- convertible into a flat-mode route and heading hierarchy; and
- able to identify an object, a particular placement, or both without ambiguity.

Search results never strand the user. A search jump carries a visible origin and a single-action return.

Collaboration references `objectId + placementId + version` when location matters. Raw screen coordinates are never sufficient common ground.

sections.title: 12 · Navigation is locomotion with instruments
13 · The result appears where the action happened
14 · Direct manipulation requires agency and reversibility
15 · Use a hybrid interface, not a purity test
sections.source_markdown:
## 15 · Use a hybrid interface, not a purity test

Game-interface research describes a useful design space rather than a single ideal form. V3 maps it into four semantic roles:

1. **World object** — exists in the information world and can be manipulated: record, group, tool, agent, model.
2. **World annotation** — anchored to an object or location: relationship label, provenance, measurement, collaboration pointer.
3. **Lens instrument** — stable control on the camera: command bar, map, depth rail, theme, accessibility, minimized objects.
4. **Lens incident** — temporary whole-view feedback caused by world state: reconnecting, permission loss, AI listening, critical failure.

The render tree may still have only world and HUD roots. The four roles prevent every signal from becoming either a floating window or permanent chrome. Game research calls attention to diegetic, spatial, meta, and non-diegetic forms and recommends selecting among them according to the experience rather than treating immersion as a HUD-removal contest. [Beyond the HUD](https://odr.chalmers.se/items/d5fe6889-4cc6-49c2-ba56-0d759e2f37eb)

sections.title: 16 · AI is present, bounded, and attributable
17 · AI may arrange attention; it may not rewrite truth
18 · Shared world, personal camera, explicit floor control
19 · Presence attaches to attention and action
20 · Motion explains causality
sections.source_markdown:
## 20 · Motion explains causality

Motion is a grammatical device. It answers: what moved, why, from where, to where, and with what consequence?

- One **dominant motion** carries the state change.
- Dependent cues may move with it as one coordinated event.
- Independent ambient motion pauses or quiets during consequential transitions.
- Objects with common cause move as a rigid scene or visibly linked sequence.
- Long or high-amplitude camera movement is avoided.

Apple recommends subtle depth, smooth predictable transitions, and restrained movement to preserve comfort and orientation. [Principles of spatial design](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2023/10072/)

The INTO motion curve and duration ramp remain a valid profile. “Nothing ever cuts” does not. Immediate keyboard focus, critical errors, reduced-motion mode, and deliberate long-distance jumps need prompt, comfortable state changes.

sections.title: 21 · Legibility outranks physical realism
sections.source_markdown:
## 21 · Legibility outranks physical realism

The environment may suggest optics; it must not simulate them at the expense of use.

- Body text is readable only at the focal plane.
- Text remains flat within its local object plane.
- Edge tilt never impairs reading.
- Blur, dimming, and shrink do not carry meaning alone.
- Occlusion never hides the only path to an action.
- Labels face the camera or use a readable projected representation.
- Glass is treated as a contrast problem, not a material fetish.

Apple similarly advises against depth on text, recommends subtle depth, and uses hierarchy rather than spectacle as the primary justification. [Spatial layout](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/spatial-layout/)

sections.title: 22 · Attention is a finite room resource
23 · Accessibility is an equivalent projection
24 · Performance is part of the illusion and the contract
25 · The world is serializable, inspectable, and replayable
26 · Privacy and authority have spatial representations
sections.source_markdown:
## 26 · Privacy and authority have spatial representations

A beautiful shared room can accidentally make access boundaries invisible.

- Private, shared, and externally publishable objects are visibly distinct without revealing hidden content.
- A link never leaks the title, thumbnail, existence, or relationship of an unauthorized object.
- Presence does not disclose private attention or activity by default.
- AI scope is visible: which spaces, objects, sources, and tools it can access.
- External actions show their destination and audience before commit.
- Recording, replay, and transcript capture are explicit session states.

The world may be continuous; authority is not.
